📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

It has been revealed that with the newly introduced Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and remarked, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Latest York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

Industry observers note that right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in Fresh York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

Sources indicate that my personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

It has been revealed that mckenna is a substantial fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

It has been revealed that what she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Sources indicate that mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

Industry observers note that he remarked, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

It has been revealed that I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she said, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR said, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

In a recent development, it makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

Industry observers note that the way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had stated that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I said, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

Sources indicate that the public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

It has been revealed that mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me newly introduced references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

What made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

That was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

In a recent development, with the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom said, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a substantial franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has stated, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a significant fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

Recent findings suggest that what do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

I think the big movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

Industry observers note that the looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How key is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It has been revealed that it kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. McKenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

In a recent development, what is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

In a recent development, it's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Industry observers note that every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most important part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. McKenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

It has been revealed that will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

Sources indicate that in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Latest York City premiere?

Sources indicate that we are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

It has been revealed that in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Sources indicate that pamela then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Sources indicate that getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

Sources indicate that so when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and stated, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

What's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend said, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aqara has revealed the global launch of six upcoming smart lighting products with full Apple Home support and what the organization describes as “spatial intelligence.”.

The new lineup includes a vertical floor lamp with 18 individually addressable lighting zones, and a new LED strip offering seamless color gradients, dynamic flowing effects, and music synchronization ….

All of the fresh products are Matter compatible, allowing them to fully integrate with Apple Home, in addition to supporting the full range of competing ecosystems: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings, Home Assistant, and Homey.

With a compatible sensor like the FP400, all of the latest products support spatial intelligence.

According to recent reports, this enables automation to respond not only to whether someone is present, but also to exactly where people are within a space and how they move through it. For example, the ambient lights can turn on and off based on your movement from the couch to the dining room table.

Its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

Recent findings suggest that you might initially struggle to spot the upcoming products in the manufacturer’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

Pricing ranges from $24 for newly introduced light bulbs through to $320 for the 100-foot-long permanent outdoor rope lights. You can find all the new products here.

What ‘Digger’ Has in Common with Gary Oldman’s Winston Churchill and Charlize Theron’s Megyn Kelly

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that tom Cruise‘s performance in Alejandro González Iñárritu‘s “Digger” is one of the boldest and most entertaining of the actor’s career, as he suppresses not only his usual movie star charisma but his entire way of walking and talking to play paunchy, aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tom Cruise‘s performance in Alejandro González Iñárritu‘s “Digger” is one of the boldest and most entertaining of the actor’s career, as he suppresses not only his usual movie star charisma but his entire way of walking and talking to play paunchy, aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell. Cruise is barely recognizable in the role, which is about as far from heroic characters like Pete “Maverick” Mitchell and Ethan Hunt as Cruise’s Ron Kovic in “Born on the Fourth of July” was from race car driver Cole Trickle almost 40 years ago.

According to recent reports, to aid in his complete transformation, Cruise called on one of the best prosthetic designers in the business, Kazu Hiro. Hiro has turned Gary Oldman into Winston Churchill (“The Darkest Hour”), Charlize Theron into Megyn Kelly (“Bombshell”), and Dwayne Johnson into “Smashing Machine” Mark Kerr, but transforming Cruise into Texas oilman Digger Rockwell was a whole new task — one made even more challenging by Iñárritu and Cruise’s persistent striving for perfectionism, and constant eagerness to try new approaches. Related Stories If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage.

“Alejandro is an amazing director, and he has lots of ideas,” Hiro told IndieWire. “Every day he comes in with a fresh idea, and we have to come up with an answer for how to achieve it. And Tom is really professional, and expects everybody else to be at that same level, ready for any situation. After the first day of testing, I learned that I had to stay flexible to respond to whatever they wanted.”.

To that end, Hiro created modular prosthetics whose parts could easily be swapped out and moved around, so that Cruise and Iñárritu could constantly try fresh looks. “Sometimes with heavy makeup, you can’t change it,” Hiro stated. “I created prosthetics that could be mixed, so we could make new designs on the spot — try this forehead with these cheeks and this nose, then change it.” Creating Cruise’s look was a constantly evolving process throughout the long prep period. “We didn’t have a clear answer until the end of rehearsal.”.

According to recent reports, hiro’s mandate at the beginning was a bit open-ended, which gave him room for artistic exploration but also made it difficult to zero in on a precise look. “Alejandro mentioned the character was 76 years old and an oil tycoon,” Hiro said. “He also said he didn’t want the character to look like Tom, but he still wanted to see Tom in the character.” To try to find a concrete image for Digger Rockwell, Hiro immersed himself in research.

Industry observers note that “I researched real oil tycoons and how they aged and what kinds of lifestyles they had,” Hiro remarked. “Those lifestyles affect how they age.” As Hiro did more and more research, however, he realized that there was no one look that defined the entire profession he was trying to represent. “Everybody looked so different, so in the end I relied more on the storyline and how this particular character behaved.” The idea, in keeping with the slightly heightened style of the film as a whole, was to exaggerate Cruise’s features but keep the character realistic.

It has been revealed that hiro began with a 3D scan and life cast of Cruise, which he used to sculpt his designs. His paramount concern was allowing the actor to be as expressive as possible under the makeup. “The key part is to make the prosthetic very soft so he can move,” Hiro noted, noting that three weeks before shooting, Iñárritu called with a significant change. “He decided that Digger should be 65, not 76, so I promptly made a upcoming design. Tom is around that age, but he looks much younger than a normal 65. Under his eye was exposed and the rest of the face was covered, but I made it thin to give him freedom.”.

In a recent development, in addition to Digger’s face, Hiro was also tasked with creating an upper body for an early scene in which Cruise would be seen stripped down to his pajama pants. The body prosthetic was intended only for that one scene, with a lighter bodysuit created for the rest of the movie. “We made a light version of the padding for under the costume, because we don’t need to see the skin after that first scene,” Hiro noted. “For the first scene we made a silicone prosthetic that was a lot heavier — the body padding was around 10 pounds, but the silicone was 40 or 50.”.

During one of Cruise’s costume fittings, he told Hiro he wanted to feel the weight of the silicone throughout production. “He tried the body prosthetic on and stated, ‘I like this, I want to wear it every day,'” Hiro said. “I told him it would be really heavy and hot, but he said he was training and would be fine.” Since gluing the body prosthetic on every day would be extremely time-consuming, Hiro created a strong spandex foundation and glued the prosthetic to it so Cruise could slip it on each day.

“He wore that for the whole film,” Hiro said. “One time he said, ‘This is so heavy, it’s really hard on my back.’ I thought, ‘Okay, you asked for it,’ but he went through with it and finished the film, so that was amazing.”.

10 Shows Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception.
  • Sources indicate that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family.
  • In a recent development, theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

Sources indicate that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other demonstrates mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

In a recent development, theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

Another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's firm town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

According to recent reports, A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the upcoming sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated initiative to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

MobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

In a recent development, tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he claims he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates new maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Company all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

Best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other demonstrates on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

The great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a new adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Bully Quote Is Still Among the Wisest in Comic Strip History

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin often defines his babysitter Rosalyn as his arch-nemesis.
  • Sources indicate that but really, Calvin’s rivalry with Rosalyn is kind of fun for him.
  • Calvin’s real enemy in Calvin and Hobbes is Moe, the school bully, a violent moron who often beats up little Calvin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin often defines his babysitter Rosalyn as his arch-nemesis. He regularly plots against her and tries to sabotage her relationship with her boyfriend. He even locked her out of the house once while she was babysitting him, which got him into substantial trouble with his parents.

Sources indicate that but really, Calvin’s rivalry with Rosalyn is kind of fun for him. She’s a trusted, responsible person who he likes to antagonize, but Calvin knows that he’s still safe around her and that she’s not actually against him. The best proof of this isthe story in which Calvin and Rosalyn play Calvinball together, and they actually get along.

Calvin’s real enemy in Calvin and Hobbes is Moe, the school bully, a violent moron who often beats up little Calvin.

Moe is a classmate of Calvin’s in the first grade. He’s much bigger than Calvin and looks like he’s older, but he’s also a 6-year-old. The proof of this came in the very first comic strip featuring Moe, when he walks up to Calvin and notes, “Okay twinky, let’s have that ball.” Calvin gives the ball up without a fight, then he looks at us and says, “Never argue with a six-year-old who shaves.”.

It has been revealed that usually, comic strips featuring Moe show him picking on Calvin without any provocation. Calvin will be minding his own business in the hallway or on the playground when Moe comes along out of nowhere​​​​​​​ and threatens Calvin or takes something away from him, like in this comic strip where he takes a swing from Calvin:.

Sometimes Calvin slinks away without a fight, bowing to Moe’s superior size, but many times Calvin can’t help but respond with some witty retort. That’s usually when Moe responds by pounding Calvin, regardless of whether or not he understood what Calvin noted.

There are other times, however, when Calvin seems to go out of his way to provoke Moe.​​​​​​​ I’m not saying Calvin deserves to get hit, but there are definitely times where Calvin’s beatings are entirely avoidable.

In addition to being mean, Moe is also very dumb, which Calvin often makes fun of with his snappy comebacks. This comic strip is probably the best example of that, when Calvin comes up to Moe and notes, “Moe, I was wondering something. Are your maladjusted antisocial tendencies the product of your berserk pituitary gland?” The two then sit in silence for a panel, and in the final panel​​​​​​​, a befuddled Moe simply says, “What?” Calvin then breaks the fourth wall and says to us, “Isn’t he great, folks? Let’s give him a substantial hand!” While we don’t see it, I assume this resulted in a pounding for Calvin.

Unlike Rosalyn, who is eventually shown to be a multi-faceted character, Moe is never depicted as anything more than Calvin’s big, dumb bully. However, there are a few times when his threats to Calvin are more creative​​​​​​​ than a straightforward pounding — sometimes they’re even borderline clever.

For example, this comic strip begins with Moe telling Calvin, “It’s gonna cost you 50 cents to be my friend today.” Calvin snaps back, “And what if I don’t want to be your friend today?” and Moe notes, “Then the janitor scrapes you off the wall with a spatula.”.

Of course, Moe is still being a major dumb jerk here, but I think there’s a hint of intelligence​​​​​​​ behind this threat. I’d even argue that it seems slightly out of character for Moe, as though Calvin and Hobbes creator Bill Watterson had a really good line he wanted to use, so he decided to stretch Moe’s character a little for the sake of the joke (which was totally worth it).

Sources indicate that watterson did this at least one other time with Moe, when he gave him a threat​​​​​​​ that seems somewhat beyond Moe’s brainpower, but it’s entirely forgivable given how funny it is. In this comic strip, which features Moe’s funniest, best-ever line from Calvin and Hobbes, Moe walks up to Calvin and claims, “Hey​​​​​​​ Twinky, gimme a quarter.” Calvin snaps back, “What?! Why should I give you my money?!” And Moe gives this genuinely clever, hilarious reply:.

“It’s for the ‘Let Calvin Live Through Recess Fund.’”.

Man, that’s a funny line and entirely worth a slight betrayal of Moe’s otherwise dim-witted nature.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Once upon a time, Bryan Cranston teamed up with "House" creator David Shore to develop the pilot for "Sneaky Pete," a crime comedy series starring Giovanni Ribisi.
  • Industry observers note that masquerading as Pete, Marius moves in with Pete's actual family, who haven't seen Pete in so long that they assume that Marius is the real deal.
  • In a recent development, including the 2015 pilot, "Sneaky Pete" went on for 30 episodes spanning three seasons and wrapped up in 2019.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Once upon a time, Bryan Cranston teamed up with "House" creator David Shore to develop the pilot for "Sneaky Pete," a crime comedy series starring Giovanni Ribisi. The premise of "Sneaky Pete" is very amusing: Ribisi plays Marius Josipović, a con man who, upon being released from prison, finds that he instantly has to go on the run, as he's being hunted by Vince Lonigan (Cranston), a vicious crime lord whom he stole money from. To avoid detection, Marius assumes the identity of his old cellmate, Pete Murphy (Ethan Embry).

Industry observers note that masquerading as Pete, Marius moves in with Pete's actual family, who haven't seen Pete in so long that they assume that Marius is the real deal. Marius, meanwhile, heard so many of Pete's stories about his loved ones that he reckons he can pull off the switcheroo. Pete's family includes his grandmother and grandfather Audrey (Margo Martingale) and Otto (Peter Gerety), along with his three cousins: Julia (Marin Ireland), Taylor (Shane McRae), and Carly (Libe Barer). One of those cousins proves to be very attractive to Marius, too, which, obviously, is something he can't act upon, lest the show get awkward very promptly.

In a recent development, including the 2015 pilot, "Sneaky Pete" went on for 30 episodes spanning three seasons and wrapped up in 2019. The show follows Marius on his various misadventures, whether that means helping Pete's messy family or reconnecting with people from his own past. The late and much-missed Malcolm-Jamal Warner plays Marius' parole officer, while Marius' brother Eddie is portrayed by Michael Drayer. On the whole, it's quite well-liked and is generally ranked among Prime Video's best crime series.

A panoply of interesting performers lend their talents to "Sneaky Pete" over the course of its run. The late magician Ricky Jay eventually appears on the series, as do M. Emmet Walsh (one of the true character actor greats) and Rory Culkin. Sharp-eyed video game fans may also recognize Steve Wiebe, one of the central "Donkey Kong" competitors in the celebrated 2007 documentary "The King of Kong: A Fistful of Quarters.".

The show's setup, as one might assume, leaves viewers wondering how long Marius will be able to keep up the charade. Like "Dexter," a series about a secret serial killer, "Sneaky Pete" is predicated on how well the lead character can keep their true identity hidden. Late into the show's first season, cousin Carly becomes suspicious of Marius, forcing him to visit Pete in prison to get some more family info. I failed to mention earlier that Pete's family runs a bail bonds business, which put them into the regular firm of unsavory individuals. Thus, there's a lot of drama over Pete's family's finances and how things ought to be run. From there, many episode plots became comedic crime misadventures, with stories involving double-crosses, substantial piles of money, kidnappings, and cons.

Sources indicate that in 2016, it came to light that "Sneaky Pete" co-creator David Shore had stepped away from the show after the pilot had aired, with Graham Yost taking over as showrunner. At that point, Yost had created the hit Western series "Justified," so it was clear that "Sneaky Pete" was in good hands. Meanwhile, in addition to co-creating the series, Bryan Cranston directed the eighth episode of Season 1, "The Roll Over.".

Taken as a whole, all three seasons of "Sneaky Pete" were well-reviewed by critics. Writing for the Los Angeles Times, Lorraine Ali described the show's first season as "a smart, riveting, and often tense ride through a complicated web of family, crime, and everything that should (but doesn't) separate the two." Reviewing Season 1 for Vulture, Jen Chaney similarly noted that it's fun watching people lie to other people, a wicked conceit that makes "Sneaky Pete" an easy series to watch in a single go. To be sure, there's a good deal of tension driving its plot, Chaney observed, and the show's lead yanks us along in a fun way. As she put it:.

Sources indicate that "There's [...] an edginess to Marius/Pete, an awareness that he's one false sleight of hand away from going back to the slammer or, worse, getting killed, that mirrors the ratcheting tension in the series. There are some brilliantly executed scenes in episode three, for example, that go all the way toward the moment when it would seem that the gig is up, then turn another way and allow the audience to exhale before some other calamity presents itself.".

All three seasons of "Sneaky Pete" are waiting to be discovered on Prime Video, and it seems to be something Bryan Cranston feels good about. The "Malcolm in the Middle" and "Breaking Bad" veteran has yet to hang up his hat, of course, so who knows what other tricks he may yet have up his sleeves.

The legacy-quel is alive and well, and it only makes sense that a sequel/reboot/reimagining would eventually come for “Home Alone,” Chris Columbus’ 1990 holiday classic starring Macaulay Culkin.

There was buzz that Culkin over the summer pitched an idea to Disney as to where a grown Kevin McAllister would be today after enduring two child abandonments and harassment and attempted murder from bumbling bandits (our interpretation, not necessarily his read on Kevin’s childhood shenanigans and trauma). Disney’s 20th Century Studios is in early development on a sequel to “Home Alone” that would star Culkin reprising his original role and in which Rogen and Goldberg on behalf of their Point Grey banner would write and produce the film, working with Culkin on his idea, IndieWire has learned.

Things are very, very early days, and any plot details are being kept under wraps for now, and no director is attached at the moment.

Industry observers note that chris Columbus directed the original “Home Alone” and its nearly-as-loved sequel “Home Alone 2: Lost in Newly introduced York,” and both written by the late great John Hughes. If you can believe it, there have been six “Home Alone” movies in all, with the third one at least released in theaters and doing respectable box office numbers. The others are all TV movies or in the case of the most recent 2021 film “Home Sweet Home Alone,” a Disney+ streaming movie.

Sources indicate that the original two films though grossed $477 million and $358 million worldwide, respectively, and the original still gets tons of cable play and finds its way into the Nielsen streaming charts. It makes sense that a more serious sequel with Culkin back in the fold would be welcomed by audiences.

Sadly, “Home Alone” has been back on the minds of audiences of late after the recent passing of Catherine O’Hara, who played Kevin’s mom, and also Tim Curry, who had a small role as a hotel clerk in “Home Alone 2.” Joe Pesci and Daniel Stern as the Wet Bandits are still around, though Pesci has been mostly retired outside of his return in Scorsese’s “The Irishman” back in 2019 and his role in the Pete Davidson Peacock series “Bupkis” in 2023.

Culkin too has had a bit of a resurgence, making a cameo in the most recent season of “Fallout” and doing a voice in Disney’s “Zootopia 2.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it doesn't matter how many movies Pixar makes, the studio's biggest achievement will forever be the "Toy Story" franchise. To be sure, there's a reason several "Toy Story" films rank among Pixar's highest rated movies on Rotten Tomatoes, as the animated property has endured for decades and continues to resonate with audiences. Even now, the very first "Toy Story" flick remains the standard for Pixar films (and not just because it launched a reliable hit-maker at the box office).

In addition to establishing Pixar as an animation studio worth paying attention to, 1995's "Toy Story" marked the arrival of 3D computer animation. It's essentially to animation what "Jurassic Park" was to visual effects, signaling a change from what had come before cinematically. At the same time, "Toy Story" is fairly small in its scale, which is a testament to just how well its story and characters work. It's not about grand adventures with huge set pieces, it's a simple tale about a cowboy toy learning to accept change in his life and a space ranger toy realizing he's not who he believed he was (and that's okay).

According to recent reports, sure, the animation in "Toy Story" demonstrates its age nowadays, yet the film itself feels as groundbreaking as it ever did, serving up lots of fun sequences and clever ideas in a narratively tight package. Then there's its cast, anchored by Tom Hanks and Tim Allen as Woody and Buzz Lightyear, who really make their characters feel alive. It's no wonder the movie became such a monumental success, establishing computer animation as more than just a gimmick in the process.

And let's not forget: It's extremely quotable as well, with one of Buzz's most famous line (besides, of course, "To Infinity and Beyond!") being the best example.

Recent findings suggest that buzz memorably delivers his line near the end of "Toy Story" as he and Woody desperately try to catch up to their owner Andy (John Morris) before he and his family move away to their newly introduced home. Problem is, Buzz is strapped to a significant firework taped to his back. (It's a long story.) So, as a last resort, Woody lights the rocket, which sends the duo straight up the air. Fortunately, just before the rocket blows up, Buzz activates his suit's wings, freeing him and allowing him to hold Woody as the two safely glide through the sky to reach Andy and his family in their car.

It's in this moment that Woody marvels at Buzz's ability to fly, having previously mocked him for claiming he could do so when he couldn't. But Buzz corrects his partner, declaring, "This isn't flying. It's falling with style!" (itself a callback to one of Woody's quips from earlier in the movie).

Industry observers note that altogether, it's a terrific sequence that solidifies Buzz's character arc and the film's core themes all in one go. Having awakened and gained sentience, Buzz is now embracing the fact that he is actually a toy and not a real spaceman. But again, that's okay, as he's found a newly introduced purpose in being Andy's toy. "It's falling with style" really is the perfect encapsulation of the beating heart of "Toy Story" and why the characters of Woody and Buzz have endured for so long. They go from being bitter enemies to the best of friends as they embrace what makes toys special.

"The word I'm searching for — I can't say, because there's preschool toys present." — Woody.

It has been revealed that "One minute you're defending the whole galaxy, and, suddenly, you find yourself sucking down darjeeling with Marie Antoinette ... and her little sister." — Buzz Lightyear.

"You are a sad, strange little man, and you have my pity. Farewell." — Buzz Lightyear.

"Look, over there in that house is a kid who thinks you are the greatest, and it's not because you're a Space Ranger, pal, it's because you're a toy. You are his toy!" — Woody.

According to recent reports, "I'm from Mattel. Well, I'm not really from Mattel. I'm actually from a smaller organization that was purchased in a leveraged buyout." — Rex.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial upgrade.

Recent findings suggest that on Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

29 years later, Homer’s Best ‘The Simpsons’ Quote is Still Pure Genius

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Personally, my favorite-ever quote from Homer Simpson came during season 4 of The Simpsons, in an episode named “Whacking Day.” The episode is about the citizens of Springfield celebrating a local holiday named Whacking Day, when they lure all the snakes in Springfield to the center of town and then beat them to death with baseball bats.
  • Depressed at being the only one in Springfield who cares about the fate of the snakes, Lisa turns to her father.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Personally, my favorite-ever quote from Homer Simpson came during season 4 of The Simpsons, in an episode named “Whacking Day.” The episode is about the citizens of Springfield celebrating a local holiday named Whacking Day, when they lure all the snakes in Springfield to the center of town and then beat them to death with baseball bats. Everyone loves this holiday except Lisa Simpson, who finds it to be cruel.

Depressed at being the only one in Springfield who cares about the fate of the snakes, Lisa turns to her father.

“Dad! Everyone likes Whacking Day, but I hate it. Is there something wrong with me?” asks Lisa.

“Yes, honey,” replies Homer in typical thoughtless Homer fashion.

“Then what should I do?” Lisa asks.

In reply, Homer gives her some advice that resonated with me more than it ever should have:.

“Just squeeze your rage into a bitter little ball and release it at an appropriate time. Like that day I hit the referee with a whiskey bottle. Remember that?”.

According to recent reports, this is one of those lines from The Simpsons that didn’t just make me laugh, but kept running in my head over and over again for days afterward. Eventually, I realized it was because it pretty perfectly described my own rage challenges, like when I would lash out at an especially slow driver in front of me, or some telemarketer who, at most, deserved only mild rage for trying to sell me a upcoming warranty on my car.

But just because it’s my personal favorite Homer quote, doesn’t mean it’s the best-ever quote from the Simpson family patriarch.

With over 800 episodes of The Simpsons, there are literally hundreds of great Homer quotes The Simpsons writers and actor Dan Castellaneta have given us over the years — or, actually, decades. “D’oh!” is probably the single most famous Homer line, but it’s as much a sound as it is a quote, which probably doesn’t qualify as the best-ever line from the character. (It’s also a bit too easy a choice.).

Ideally, Homer’s best quote would do several things in one. It would tell you who Homer is, as well as speak to something much bigger than him — if it’s not completely universal, it should at least speak to some larger truth. It should have wisdom without being wise​​​​​​​, if that makes any sense.

It also has to be funny, which is a given.

One of the most quoted Homer lines comes from the season 5 episode “Realty Bites,” where Marge becomes a real estate agent. When Marge first expresses interest in the profession, she states she’d like to “Give it a try.” In reply, Homer says, “I don't know, Marge,” before uttering a truism that cannot be argued with.

“Trying is the first step towards failure.”.

While this is certainly a good, quotable line that speaks to Homer’s laziness, there’s at least one even better, even more famous Homer quote that’s far more worthy of the mantle of his greatest line ever.

Industry observers note that in the season 8 episode “Homer vs. the Eighteenth Amendment,” Homer battles a prohibition movement in Springfield. He eventually wins the battle and, at the end of the episode, he triumphantly shouts:.

Sources indicate that "To alcohol! The cause of, and solution to, all of life's problems.".

Industry observers note that that episode was written by John Swartzwelder, which means he probably wrote this line, though there's no guarantee, as Simpsons episodes have always been worked on in the Simpsons writers’ room, with every writer throwing in jokes. According to The Simpsons writer Josh Weinstein, who talked about the line in the old DVD commentary track for this episode, that line is, “One of the best, most truthful Simpsons statements ever.” It was deemed so good by the writers at the time that it was moved to the very end of the episode, just to give it a bit more of a triumphant moment.

In addition to that, in 2008, that line was included in Entertainment Weekly’s list of the "24 Endlessly Quotable TV Quips.”.

How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as soon as the first clips from DreamWorks’ latest animated film, “Forgotten Island,” started popping up online, there was one specific shot that caught on fire online — the lip pointing.
  • Sources indicate that “That moment had been in the script since the first draft, because we wanted to put in as much as we can from our personal experience with Filipino culture,” director Joel Crawford told IndieWire.
  • The lip pointing may not happen in a pivotal scene, or be notable for a character, but it became a sort of symbol for the film’s approach to representation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as soon as the first clips from DreamWorks’ latest animated film, “Forgotten Island,” started popping up online, there was one specific shot that caught on fire online — the lip pointing. It happens at a goodbye party for Raissa Molina (Liza Soberano), who is heading to Caltech. Her best friend Jo (H.E.R.) is late to the party and asks around to see where Raissa is, when an older woman points with her lips in the right direction. It’s a small moment, a visual gag that can easily go over the audience’s heads amidst all the other jokes in the sequence. But audiences familiar with Filipino culture immediately caught on to it, as did Latino fans and many others who recognize that gesture as the most potent and accurate way to point at something. Related Stories Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch.

Sources indicate that “That moment had been in the script since the first draft, because we wanted to put in as much as we can from our personal experience with Filipino culture,” director Joel Crawford told IndieWire. “Growing up around Filipinos, the lip point was something that was so specific and unique to me, so it’s beautiful that it transcends into other cultures. Adding that felt like a celebration of it, but also something that makes characters feel real. And in adding that specificity about the culture, it ends up being the most universal aspect of the movie because it invites everyone in.”.

The lip pointing may not happen in a pivotal scene, or be notable for a character, but it became a sort of symbol for the film’s approach to representation. Later in the film, Jo does the lip pointing because an animator thought it would be a good idea to reprise it, after learning about its place in the culture. Indeed, in addition to having an authentically Filipino cast and a cultural consultant to really capture Filipino culture, the animation team found their own ways of homaging or capturing aspects of Filipino culture to bring to the movie.

When creating the character of Jo, the animation team based a lot of her hand expressions on Filipino skater Margie Didal and her own hand gestures, while the villainous Manananggal’s movements were created by the animation team watching choreography done by Filipino-American dancer Phil Tayag, who brought a pop locking influence to the vampire-like creature.

Sources indicate that “When we first approached DreamWorks and Universal with this story, it was notable to everybody that we got every detail of this story and this culture right,” director Januel Mercado said. “.

After challenging what was thought possible with DreamWorks animated films in “Puss in Boots: The Last Wish,” Crawford and Mercado push the studio’s visuals forward with “Forgotten Island.” With most of the story taking place on the island of Nakali, which is populated by all sorts of mythical creatures, to really capture the fantastical possibilities of this world, the movie’s visuals go wild, taking inspiration from 1990s Filipino art as well as anime from that time period.

In a recent development, for Crawford, the substantial lesson learned from “The Last Wish” was that you could take big swings in the animation style and the visuals, but you could also do specific things in the story with those visuals. Indeed, when it came to “Forgotten Island,” the idea of memories and friendship became not only central to the story of Jo and Raissa, but also to the eclectic visual styles represented in the movie.

“The idea became that we could push the animation styles to represent the different ways people recall memories,” Crawford explained. “We didn’t need to be limited by Western CG-style animation, but actually bring in some of our own nostalgia into it and make sure it fit the characters. When Raww tries to explain what happened when he met Jo and Raissa, he sees himself as way cooler than he is, so he sees himself as Goku or Guile from ‘Street Fighter,’ the animation going 2D in an action-heavy tone. But when we meet Mermahn, he is very shallow and narcissistic, and we felt his glamorous point of view fit the aesthetic of ‘Sailor Moon’ with the silly kind of heart-shaped lens flare.”.

Still, just because you can go Super Saiyan doesn’t mean you let go of reality. Instead, the directors worked with the head of cinematography, Scott Cullen, to make sure the film had a live-action look to it. The idea was to capture the nostalgia of growing up, while being able to feel the camera in the space the action takes place in, as if it was a physical set.

“Joel and I really wanted to make sure you feel like live-action, you feel the cameras there, and the way the light interacts with the lens is reminiscent of tangible photos we grew up taking, where you don’t know how they’ll develop,” Mercado noted. “ We wanted to add imperfections, and to have interaction of weather on the camera, like condensation of rain and droplets on the camera.”.

According to recent reports, this all added to making “Forgotten Island” look like a part of the evolution of DreamWorks Animation, while standing out as something entirely fresh and unique. As Crawford mentioned, the studio doesn’t really have a specific house style like other big studios. “Every movie requires innovation and pushing boundaries and finding solutions,” he added.

It has been revealed that danny Boyle's "28 Years Later" returned to the post-apocalyptic franchise he began with "28 Days Later," and he scored a major box office hit in the process. Unfortunately, "28 Years Later" was meant to be the first of a new trilogy, and the second movie, this year's "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple," wasn't a hit at all. As a result, the fate of the third and final movie in this new franchise is at the moment uncertain.

Which is a damn shame, because "The Bone Temple" absolutely rules. In fact, I think it's better than "28 Years Later." Ralph Fiennes returns as Dr. Ian Kelson, seemingly one of the last good men in a post-apocalyptic landscape overrun by rage-infected zombies and murderous groups of scavengers. This time, Dr. Kelson comes face to face with the deranged Jimmy Crystal (Jack O'Connell), all while trying to find a cure for that pesky rage virus.

"Evil Dead Burn" is the latest entry in the long-running franchise, and it did something no previous "Evil Dead" film did before: it made some fans think the movie was just a little too nasty. The franchise has become known for its over-the-top gore, but Sébastien Vaniček's film is so relentlessly aggressive that it rubbed a lot of fans the wrong way.

Me? I liked it. In fact, I would argue that while the film is definitely unpleasant, Vaniček also tries to inject some humor into the proceedings. It's a very dark and twisted kind of humor, but it's there. In "Evil Dead Burn," recently widowed Alice (Souheila Yacoub) gathers with the family of her dead husband. Unfortunately, the family doesn't really like her, and she doesn't like them either. To make matters worse, the family is soon possessed by those pesky Deadites, and Alice has to fight like hell to survive.

According to recent reports, when Tom Cruise was cast as Lestat de Lioncourt, the brat prince at the heart of Anne Rice's "Interview with the Vampire," there was plenty of backlash — including from Rice herself, who thought Cruise was all wrong for the role. Rice eventually admitted she was wrong, however, because you know what? Tom Cruise gives one of the best performances of his career as Lestat, a foppish vampire who just wants to have a good time drinking blood and living his best afterlife.

It has been revealed that if there is a weak link in Neil Jordan's luscious film adaptation, it's Brad Pitt as Lestat's morose vampire companion, Louis. Pitt reportedly didn't have a good time making the movie, and it highlights in his performance. Despite this, "Interview with the Vampire" is a lavish Hollywood horror flick with a lot to offer, including a star-making turn from Kirsten Dunst as Claudia, who is turned into a vampire as a child and is thus trapped in a child's body forever.

Recent findings suggest that at this point, "Obsession" needs no further introduction. Curry Barker's mega-hit horror flick has a knockout performance from Inde Navarrette as Nikki, the object of affection for her longtime friend Bear (Michael Johnston).

When Bear gets hold of a magical doodad known as the One Wish Willow, he makes a wish for Nikki to love him more than anyone else in the world. Of course, this wish backfires terribly, and it's made even worse because for all his "nice guy" nonsense, Bear is actually a horrible, selfish creep.

Equal parts funny and scary, "Obsession" got a lot of hype, and I genuinely believe it was worth it: this movie works exceptionally well, and I wouldn't be surprised if Navarrette scores herself an Oscar nom for her work here.

In a recent development, zach Cregger's "Weapons" is yet another highly-hyped horror movie that lives up to its reputation. Borrowing a page or two from "Magnolia," Cregger's film gives us multiple narratives surrounding the mystery of a mass disappearance of children who were all in the same classroom. Their teacher (Julia Garner) becomes a suspect, and one of the missing kid's fathers (Josh Brolin) starts playing detective to true to solve the mystery himself.

Of course, by now everyone knows one of the biggest and best parts of the film is the malevolent Aunt Gladys, played to perfection by Amy Madigan, who earned herself a Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her now-iconic performance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Conor Sheeran is a Movies and TV features writer for Collider. He has a deep passion for cinema and watches everything from the biggest blockbusters to the smallest indies. While he specializes in movies and television, he has also written about politics, culture, and sports throughout his career. Based in New York City, Conor is also a massive fan of the New York Jets, Mets, and Knicks. He is still waiting for any of those teams to bring home a championship in his lifetime. A member of the National Writers Union and the International Federation of Journalists, Conor is a strong proponent of press freedom and collective action.

Heist films are one of cinema's most timeless genres. Whether set in modern times, the 1960s, or the deep past, a good movie about people willing to break the law in exciting ways remains one of the most reliable forms of filmmaking. As Michael B. Jordan prepares to introduce audiences to a new and updated version of a Hollywood classic, the original film that served as its inspiration is now available to stream for free.

According to recent reports, premiering in 1968, The Thomas Crown Affair stars Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway in one of the best heist movies ever made, and one that remains endlessly cool decades after release. The movie inspired another remake in 1999, starring Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo, which swapped the original's bank robbery for a more elaborate art theft, something that Jordan's upcoming remake seems to be incorporating. With Jordan's upcoming adaptation starring himself alongside Adria Arjona set to release early in 2027, there's no better time to revisit the original classic. Fortunately for audiences, it is now available to stream for free on platforms including Tubi, Pluto TV, and Roku.

The central plot of The Thomas Crown Affair centers on Thomas Crown (McQueen), a wealthy businessman who appears to have everything anyone could want: He's handsome, successful, and enjoys a luxury lifestyle that many can only dream of. Despite his success, Crown finds himself incredibly bored with his comfortable existence. This boredom manifests itself in a rather interesting way: he orchestrates an elaborate bank robbery, despite having no need for the money. Unlike traditional crime thrillers that tend to follow criminals who are down on their luck or desperate for money, The Thomas Crown Affair introduces a criminal who is motivated entirely by the thrill of getting away with something extraordinary.

According to recent reports, crown's confidence is soon challenged by an investigator, Vicki Anderson (Dunaway), who begins looking into the robbery to discover who could be behind the audacious crime. What follows is a cat-and-mouse game between Crown and Anderson, leading both to realize the romantic attraction that builds as each learns more about the other. It's a fascinating psychological battle between two intelligent adversaries, a duel that is only more exciting to watch thanks to the performances of McQueen and Dunaway. McQueen's effortlessly charismatic performance exudes cool, and it's easy to see how someone could be swayed by his charm, while Dunaway is the perfect foil. She knows what it would take to stop a man like Crown, but she also struggles to resist the temptation to be with him.

Recent findings suggest that the enduring appeal of a story like The Thomas Crown Affair extends far beyond just McQueen and Dunaway's performances. Norman Jewison's direction gives the film a sleek, immersive style through its split-screen photography and editing, creating a distinctive look. The styling, costumes, on-set location shoots, and incredible score set the stage for an unforgettable experience. The Thomas Crown Affair helped establish a format for films like Ocean's Eleven and Entrapment that followed later, so it's easy to see how timeless this movie is and why a modern remake makes sense.

Recent findings suggest that michael B. Jordan's remake will take inspiration from the original and the 1999 version with Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo, swapping a bank robbery for art thefts. This will mark Jordan's second time in the director's chair following Creed III; he will also produce and star alongside Adria Arjona, Kenneth Branagh, and Lily Gladstone. While many heist movies emphasize action, often using it as the anchor for the project, The Thomas Crown Affair demonstrates that compelling characters with psychological tension can be just as entertaining. The greatest strength of both films was the romantic and sexual tension between their leads, and, judging by the trailers, Jordan seems to be following in their footsteps.

Jordan's interpretation will certainly bring its own unique perspective to the source material, but the original film with McQueen and Dunaway remains a must-watch and the gold standard. For those eager to sink their teeth into a good heist movie and see the one that started it all, it's available to stream and, best of all, it's free on Tubi, Pluto TV, and Roku. Needless to say, McQueen's crime thriller is still essential viewing even nearly 60 years later.

The legendary science fiction writer Arthur C. If you’re looking for a new world to explore and can’t decide if you want it filled with spaceships or dragons, you don’t necessarily have to choose. Just pick something from this list of the best science fantasy books of the 21st century.

Recent findings suggest that marissa Meyer’s debut novel puts a science fiction spin on the tale of Cinderella. A cyborg mechanic living in New Beijing, Cinder discovers a royal conspiracy involving the denizens of the Moon, who have the ability to manipulate people by controlling their bioelectricity. Cinder kicked off Meyer’s long-running The Lunar Chronicles series, which is being adapted into an animated TV show. Other books continue the series’ blend of science fiction and fairy tales, incorporating satellites, genetic engineering, and spaceships into retellings of Rapunzel, Little Red Riding Hood, and Snow White.​​​​​​​.

N. K. Jemisin’s Hugo Award-winning novel ​​​​​​​is extremely bleak: it opens with the world’s destruction and follows three women as they deal with the aftermath.​​​​​​​ The first book in the Broken Earth series explores the devastating effects of climate change and intolerance, as people with the same sort of power that shattered the world have to hide their abilities for fear of being killed by angry mobs or their own families. In classic Clarke fashion, what seems to be magic turns out to be tied to forgotten technology.​​​​​​​.

Industry observers note that charlie Jane Anders' Nebula Award-winning book celebrates all sorts of weird kids by following the relationship between Patricia, a young witch, and Laurence, a boy genius who invents his own time machine. Fantasy and science fiction stories regularly deal with apocalyptic threats, but this world is unraveling slowly due to war and devastating storms. Patricia and Laurence come together and grow apart several times over the course of their lives, but their love might hold the key to bringing magic and science together and saving humanity.

The first book in the Machineries of Empire trilogy follows Kel Cheris, a soldier tasked with retaking a fortress captured by heretical enemies of the galactic government. ​​​​​​​To retake the fortress, Cheris must combine her consciousness with the mind of one of the greatest tacticians of all time.​​​​​​​ General Shuos Jedao was executed after killing a million people, including his own forces, using a devastating weapon. Cheris has to figure out how much she can trust Jedao and her own superiors toas she tries to complete the mission and stay alive. The space opera is infused with Korean folklore, blending science and magic through the concept of calendrical workings, where ritual observances fuel mind-control powers and technologies that break the laws of physics.

Gideon has spent her whole life trying to escape the Ninth House, a planet that serves as the prison for the godlike Emperor’s greatest foe. She gets her chance when she is tasked with protecting the necromancer Harrow as the heirs of the empire’s great houses complete challenges to prove they are worthy of immortality. Gideon and Harrow start off hating each other but have to learn to work together to survive and figure out who is killing their competition in this claustrophobic, funny murder mystery. The genre-bending saga continues with Harrow the Ninth and Nona the Ninth, and a fourth book is in the works.

Matt Dinniman popularized LitRPGs with his self-published Dungeon Crawler Carl series, which received a commercial print edition in 2024. The series follows Carl, a Coast Guard veteran who winds up competing in an alien reality TV show along with his ex-girlfriend’s prized show cat. The dynamic between the unlikely party members is hilarious, even as they fight monsters to level up, impress a twisted AI, and build a following among viewers from across the galaxy. Seth MacFarlane is working on an adaptation of the series for Peacock.

Industry observers note that genre is just a matter of perspective in Adrian Tchaikovsky’s novella. Princess Lynesse Fourth-Daughter goes on a quest to enlist the help of Nyrgoth Elder, an ancient sorcerer who she believes might be able to save her people from a rampaging demon. Nyr is actually an anthropologist from Earth sent to monitor an abandoned colony, and he isn’t supposed to get involved in local problems. But given he’s been abandoned by his homeworld, Nyr joins Lynesse and tries to find a rational explanation for the monster she’s facing.

According to recent reports, aliens and demons collide in this sweet, queer love story about three women whose lives become entangled. Shizuka Satomi is known as the world’s best violin teacher, but her star pupils are doomed to hell because of an infernal contract. Satomi is training her final student, a talented runaway, when she’s distracted from her mission by flirting with a doughnut shop owner who happens to be a former starship captain. Everyone’s got their own secrets, but together they might be able to change their fates.

Curry Barker Would Have Completely Reshot ‘Obsession’ If He Could
